allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer greater than 1. For which real numbers $x$ is \\[\\lfloor nx \\rfloor - \\sum_{k=1}^{n} \\frac{\\lfloor kx \\rfloor}{k}\\] maximal, and what is the maximal value that this expression can take?

payload.role_in_assembly: Reduce the maximization problem on [0,1) to the discrete endpoints a/n.

domain_restrictions: k is an integer summation index with 1 less than or equal to k and k less than or equal to n
floor is the greatest integer less than or equal to its real input
root_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For each fixed integer n greater than 1, consider the function E_n(x) = floor(n x) minus the sum over integers k with 1 <= k <= n of floor(k x) divided by k. The task is to determine the set of real x values for which E_n(x) attains its maximum over all real x, and to determine the corresponding maximal value M(n).
quantifier_order: for all integers n with n greater than 1
there exists a real number x_star

variables.name: n
variables.role: fixed parameter with constraint n greater than 1

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index, restricted to k from 1 through n

variables.name: x
variables.role: variable over which the expression is maximized

variables.name: y
variables.role: arbitrary competitor value to define maximality

variables.name: E_n(x)
variables.role: defined expression: floor(n x) minus sum from k = 1 to n of floor(k x) divided by k

variables.name: M(n)
variables.role: the maximal value of E_n(x) over all real x, depends on n

variables.name: x_star
variables.role: a real number where the maximum is achieved; may depend on n

witness_dependencies: x_star depends on n (the maximizing real numbers may vary with the given integer n)

domain_restrictions: a is defined as floor(n*t), hence a is an integer
a/n is therefore a rational number; implicit requirement that E_n is defined at argument a/n
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1, for all real numbers t with 0 <= t < 1, let a be floor(n*t); then E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).

variables.name: a
variables.role: auxiliary value defined by a = floor(n*t)

variables.domain: unspecified; takes input of the form a real number t and returns a value compared by <=
variables.name: E_n
variables.role: indexed by n; used to evaluate E_n(t) and E_n(a/n)

witness_dependencies: a depends on both n and t via a = floor(n*t)

payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with 0 <= t < 1, if a = floor(n*t), then E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).
